examples.knowledge_point: Calculating the Area of the Image of an Object Under a Linear Transformation Given a Diagram
examples.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13992537/assets/e8ff769df4089e6ed9a47d56d7317acf41b8aef6a255abc705c0e7ec31a446ea.png)

Consider the shaded region $D$ shown above. What is the area of the image of $D$ under the action of the linear transformation $\mathbf{T}$ with the standard matrix $T,$ given below?

$$
[\begin{aligned}4 & 2 \\ -1 & 2\end{aligned}]
$$
examples.worked_solution:
Recall that for any linear transformation $\mathbf{T},$ we have the following connection between the area of $D$ and the area of the image $\mathbf{T}(D)$ under the action of $\mathbf{T}\mathbin{:}$

$$
\text{Area}(\mathbf{T}(D)) = |\det(T)| \cdot \text{Area}(D)
$$

From the diagram, we have

$$
\text{Area}(D) = \frac{1}{2} \cdot 3 \cdot 4 = 6.
$$

Computing the determinant of $T,$ we get 

$$
\det(T) = 4 \cdot 2 -  2 \cdot (-1) = 10.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Area}(T(D)) & =|det(T)|\cdot \text{Area}(D) \\  & =|\,10\,|\cdot 6 \\  & =60.\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.problem:
What is the area scale factor of the linear transformation $T$ that is given by its standard matrix 

$$
T=[\begin{aligned}9 & 5 \\ 7 & 0\end{aligned}]?
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
The area scale factor of a linear transformation $T$ with standard matrix $T$ is equal to $|det(T)|.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}|det(T)| & =|9\cdot 0-5\cdot 7| \\  & =|0-35| \\  & =35.\end{aligned}
$$
